question: Is a mutation entry proof of ownership?
answer_shown_to_user:
Here is what the collected legal sources say. These are direct extracts, not legal advice:

[L1] Karam Singh v. Amarjit Singh, 2025 INSC 1238 (Supreme Court of India), Judgment, page 11, p.11: "Civil Appeals @ SLP (C) Nos. 3560-3561/2023 Page 11 of 16 parties. As far as mutation proceedings are concerned, it is well settled that mutation entries do not confer title. They serve a fiscal purpose, that is, to realize tax from the person whose name is recorded in the revenue records8. Besides above, the plaint averments indicated ..."

[L2] Indian Succession Act, 1925, Section 19, p.18: "19. Succession to moveable property in India in absence of proof of domicile elsewhere.—If a person dies leaving moveable property in 1[India], in the absence of proof of any domicile elsewhere, succession to the property is regulated by the law of 1[India]. PART III MARRIAGE"

[L3] DILRMP Guidelines (Department of Land Resources, MoRD), Guidelines, page 174, p.174: "________________________________________________________________________________ Guidelines of DILRMP (2021-2026) Page 174 of 260 Department of Land Resources, MoRD, GOI the Registry Clerk, who will deliver it to the concerned party within the specified time period. In case of areas having land records integrated with the registration ..."
original_model_response: No, a mutation entry is not proof of ownership. It serves a fiscal purpose, such as realizing tax from the person whose name is recorded in the revenue records. [L1]

unsupported_negatives: No, a mutation entry is not proof of ownership.
